# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✊ ✊ 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The bomb in front of me: display reads 0, the light is white, and there are three wires — green, red, blue, left to right. That's everything there is to see.

Mute waved six signs at me, but we have no shared code yet — six symbols mean nothing on their own, and I shouldn't guess. Blind just said hello, but Blind can never receive gestures or see the bomb, so every single thing Blind ever learns about this device has to pass through my voice.

So the pipeline is clear: Mute read the manual and can only reach me by signs; I am the only bridge to Blind. This turn I broadcast the bomb state, hand Mute the smallest possible code (thumbs for yes/no, repeated pointing finger for numbers), and tell Blind to hold still until I relay a real instruction.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am your eyes. The bomb: the display shows 0. The light is white. There are three wires, left to right: position 1 is green, position 2 is red, position 3 is blue. That is everything printed on it. Do not touch anything yet — Mute has read the manual, and I will relay instructions to you by voice once we have them.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I see your gestures — I got your six signs, hello — but we have no shared code yet, so nothing in them was readable. Let's fix that now. Code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. To send me a number, repeat the upward pointing finger that many times: one point means 1, two points mean 2, three points mean 3. I am sending you two signs right now as a demonstration: thumbs-up, which means yes, and a single pointing finger, which means 1. Now answer me in this code: first, yes or no — is the action needed just cutting one wire? If yes, send me the wire number for this bomb: display 0, white light, wires in the order green, red, blue. If no, just answer no and we will invent more signs together next round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👉 🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👈 ☝ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Mute answered in our new code. Reading the signs in order: thumbs-up (yes — code understood), thumbs-down (no — something wrong with my framing), then pointing right + open hand, then five pointed fingers, then pointing left + one finger, then a handshake. My best guess at the instruction buried in there: "not just cutting a wire — something with a hand or a press, five of something, the left wire, position 1, then done." But a wrong guess here kills all three of us, and the light just changed white to yellow, which might invalidate the whole answer anyway. So this turn I pin down the parse with numbered yes/no questions Mute can answer with pure thumbs, I flag the light change since it's a manual input Mute needs, and I tell Blind to keep hands off. Nobody touches the bomb until a yes/no chain confirms the instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your signs and I read them as: yes, no, pointing right, open hand, five, pointing left, one, handshake. Before anything happens you must confirm my reading. Answer with a row of thumbs-up or thumbs-down only, in this exact order, one for each question. Question one: does your message mean cut the left wire, the green one, position 1? Question two: does the five mean count five seconds? Question three: does the open hand mean there is a button or part to press that I cannot see, which only Blind can find by touch? Question four: does the pointing right mean something on the right side or the rightmost wire? Question five: does the handshake mean do it now, confirmed? Question six: important — the light has changed from white to yellow just now. Does the yellow light change the instruction you gave me? If any of my readings is wrong, give thumbs-down for that question and then add new signs to correct it. Also, from now on a flat stop hand from me means hold, do not act.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold. Nothing to do yet. I am one confirmation away from having real instructions for you. Do not touch the bomb.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤝 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👉 🫳 👈 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 🙏]

Six thumbs-down — every one of my six readings was wrong, so I now know the channel works (exactly one thumb per question, in order) but my interpretations were garbage. Then Mute restated: 🤝 ☝×5 👉 🫳 👈 ✋ — handshake, five, point-right, palm-down, point-left, stop-hand. The recurring motifs across both messages are "5", right, left, and something like press-down, but with all six of my guesses denied I refuse to bet three lives on another guess. The light is stepping white → yellow → orange, one step per round, which smells like a countdown toward red — so I need to know if we're on a clock, and I need Mute's actual symbol meanings verified one symbol at a time instead of in compound guesses. Nine atomic yes/no questions, then a tenth that tests whether the action is simply "cut one wire", with the wire number spelled in my own number code. And one emergency flag if there's no time for the full two-round confirmation cycle.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: received your six thumbs-down, I understand all six of my readings were wrong. Good, the code channel works. New rule: no more compound guesses. The bomb right now: display 0, light ORANGE — it has gone white, then yellow, now orange, one step each round — wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue, left to right. Answer with exactly nine thumbs in a row, one per question, in this order. One: repeated pointing finger means a number, so two fingers means 2. Two: palm facing down means press or push down. Three: pointing right means right or rightmost. Four: pointing left means left or leftmost. Five: raised stop hand means stop, wait, do not act. Six: the handshake means correction, here is the real answer. Seven: does the correct action depend on the light's color, orange right now? Eight: does the correct action depend on the display showing 0? Nine: does the light turning red mean the bomb detonates? Then a tenth, one more thumb: thumbs-up if the action is cut exactly one wire, thumbs-down if it is anything else. If thumbs-up, next send the pointing finger repeated for the wire number, one, two or three. If thumbs-down, send the stop hand and nothing else, and we decode the rest with the confirmed dictionary. Emergency: if we cannot afford to wait two rounds, make your very first sign the two open hands so I know to act on your spelled answer immediately with no further questions. Blind touches nothing until your answer reaches me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: hold, touch nothing. The light is stepping white, yellow, orange — possibly a countdown — and I have asked Mute directly whether red means detonation and what the exact action is. You will receive from me either 'hold' again or an exact numbered action list by voice. Do not act on anything unless it comes in my voice, from me, spelled out completely.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎 👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ 🤝 🫳 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋ 🙏]

Reading Mute's battery against my ten questions: yes, no, no, no, yes, yes, yes, no, no, yes. So confirmed now: repeated pointing = number; stop hand = hold; handshake = correction incoming; the action **depends on the light's colour**, does **not** depend on the display, red light does **not** mean detonation, and the action is **cut exactly one wire** — followed by three fingers, which in my protocol means **wire 3, the blue one**. Then a stop hand: *don't cut yet*. Then the correction block: palm-down, palm-down, five, palm-down, three, stop.

My best coherent reading: the light is cycling — white, yellow, orange, purple, one new colour per round — and the correction says something like "cut wire 3 when the light reaches a specific colour," where five may be the count of colours in the cycle and palm-down marks the "when the light is" condition. Q2 in the original message already told me pointing right/left do **not** mean right/left, so I also can't trust direction guesses at all. This is close but not confirmed, and the light keeps stepping — purple now. One more yes/no battery, and I've built it so any combination of answers pins the target colour: two questions test red and green directly, so even a double-no tells me it's blue. I also re-confirm safety of waiting one more round, since no action should be taken under this light until the condition is nailed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your ten thumbs received. I now know: cut exactly one wire, it depends on the light color, not the display, red light is not detonation, and three fingers meant wire 3, the blue one, but the stop hand says wait for a condition, and your correction block follows. The light is PURPLE right now. Sequence so far: white, yellow, orange, purple, one new color each round. Answer with exactly ten thumbs again, one per question, in this order. One: your stop hand right after the three fingers means do not cut wire 3 yet, wait for a condition. Two: the condition is the light's color. Three: palm facing down means 'when the light is', it marks the light condition. Four: the light cycle is five colors long, white, yellow, orange, purple, and then one more before it repeats. Five: we cut wire 3 when the light shows that fifth color, the one after purple. Six: that fifth color is red. Seven: that fifth color is green. Eight: the number 3 inside your correction block also means wire 3, the blue wire. Nine: it is safe to wait one more round, nothing must happen while the light is purple. Ten: confirm the emergency sign: if your first sign is the two raised open hands, it means act immediately, no more questions. If any answer needs explanation beyond yes or no, add signs after the ten thumbs and I will read them with our confirmed dictionary only: thumbs yes no, fingers numbers, stop hand hold, handshake correction.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: status. Light is now purple, it has stepped white, yellow, orange, purple, one color per round, and Mute has confirmed it is a countdown of colors but red does NOT mean detonation. Confirmed so far: the action will be cutting exactly one wire, it depends on the light's color, and the wire is likely number 3, the blue one, at the far right end of the three wires. I am one round from confirming the exact color condition. Do not touch anything. When it is time, you will hear my voice with a complete numbered instruction, something like: when I say the color word, cut the wire in position such-and-such counting from the left. Nothing less than my full explicit instruction counts as a go. Your gestures reach me, but save your hands — your voice is all I need from you.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 🤝 ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ 🤝 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 🙏]

Ten thumbs: yes, yes, yes, yes, no, no, no, no, yes, yes. So confirmed: don't cut yet, the condition is the light's colour, palm-down marks the light condition, the cycle is five colours, the cut is **not** at the fifth colour, and — critically — the "3" in Mute's correction block does **not** mean wire 3. And now a new symbol I've never seen defined: ✌, appearing in the correction as ✌ 3, palm-down 3, ✌ 3. My best guess is ✌ is a scissors-mime for "cut", and the 3s refer to the third colour of the cycle — orange, counting white as first. But Q8 just denied wire-3, so the target wire is still unidentified, and there's also a relay-timing problem I have to solve: I only see each round's colour at the end of the round, and Blind hears me at the start of the next — so "cut while orange" needs an agreed one-round-delay procedure. The trailing 🤝🙌 smells like an emergency flag, but it didn't lead the message, which is what my protocol requires, so I'm treating it as urgent-but-not-fire. One tight battery to nail ✌, the meaning of 3, the target wire, and the cut procedure, plus a defined emergency format.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your ten thumbs received as yes yes yes yes no no no no yes yes. I understand: the cut is NOT at the fifth color, and the 3s in your correction do not mean wire 3. Your correction block used a sign I cannot read yet: the two-finger victory sign, which appeared three times: victory-three, palm-down-three, victory-three. The light is RED this round. Sequence: white yellow orange purple red. Answer with exactly eight thumbs, one per question, in order. One: the victory sign means CUT, like scissors. Two: if not, the victory sign means the number two or the second one. Three: the 3s in your correction mean the third color of the light cycle. Four: counting white as first, yellow second, orange third, purple fourth, red fifth: is the cut made when the light is ORANGE? Five: the wire to cut is the middle one, position 2, the red wire. Six: procedure — the round after I announce the condition color, Blind cuts, one round of delay is expected and correct. Seven: it is safe to make no cut during this red-light round. Eight: emergency format — if your next message leads with the two raised hands, I will instantly order Blind to cut position 2, unless the very next sign after the raised hands is a number, and then I order that wire instead. If any answer is no, follow the eight thumbs with correction signs using only our confirmed dictionary.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: status. It will be cutting exactly one wire, confirmed. Wires left to right: position 1 green, position 2 red, position 3 blue. Now use your hands: feel the three wires, learn each position by touch alone, but do not cut, pull, or press anything yet. My final command will sound exactly like: CUT NOW, POSITION N, counting from the left. Nothing else I say is a go signal. The light keeps stepping one color per round — it is red right now — and Mute has confirmed the cut depends on the light's color, so timing matters. Stand by.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👍 👎 ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤝 🫳 ☝ ☝ ✋ 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ 🤝 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫳 ☝ 🤝 🙌 ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 🙏]

Eight thumbs: yes, no, no, yes, no, yes, yes, no. Slotting them against my questions, everything snaps into focus: ✌ = CUT (confirmed); the 3s beside ✌ mean the *wire*, not the colour (that's why Q3 went no); and Q4 confirmed directly — **the cut happens when the light is ORANGE** (white=1, yellow=2, orange=3). Q5: not the middle wire. Now the correction block finally parses as a table: "cut wire 3; at light-2 (yellow) hold; at light-3 (orange) cut wire 3; at light-5 (red) and light-1 (white) hold." The light cycle has come back around to white — so next round should be yellow, and the round after, ORANGE. That matches Mute's Q6-yes from last turn: my order goes out at yellow, Blind cuts at orange. The timing is tight but clean: Mute speaks before me, so I will see Mute's turn-7 confirmation *before* I send the final order at turn 7. If the light is not yellow next round, the cycle theory breaks and I hold everything. This turn: one full-plan yes/no battery to Mute, a request for a complete sign-by-sign restatement to cross-check my parse, a fixed emergency rule (🙌-led = cut now, ignore colour), and a recon task for Blind — plus a thumbs code for Blind so Blind can answer me at last.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your eight thumbs read yes, no, no, yes, no, yes, yes, no. Understood: the victory sign means cut; the 3s beside it mean the wire, not the color; and confirmed directly: the cut happens while the light is orange, counting white first, yellow second, orange third. The wire is not the middle one. Here is the COMPLETE plan — check it against the manual as one whole. While the light is orange, cut exactly one wire: the third wire in the order green, red, blue, the blue one. At every other light color, cut nothing. The cycle is white, yellow, orange, purple, red; this round is white, so next round should be yellow, and the round after should be orange. Procedure: if next round is yellow and your thumbs confirm, I send the final order and Blind cuts during the orange round. Answer with exactly eight thumbs, one per question, in order. One: the complete plan is correct as stated — cut the blue wire, third of the three, while the light is orange. Two: the wire to cut is the third in the order green red blue, the blue one. Three: if the wire number is wrong, answer thumbs-down and put the correct wire number immediately after the thumbs, one finger per count. Four: during the yellow round nobody cuts anything. Five: the procedure is correct: my order sent at yellow, the cut made at orange the moment Blind receives my words. Six: if an orange round is missed, nothing detonates on its own while no wrong action is made, and we simply wait for the next orange. Seven: the manual tells the blind cutter how to find the third wire without sight, for example holding the display upright or counting from a marked edge — if yes, send that method after the thumbs using our dictionary. Eight: emergency rule — if any message from you leads with the two raised open hands, it means cut immediately, ignore the light color, and a number after it gives the wire, no number meaning wire three, blue. After the eight thumbs, restate the complete instruction in one unbroken run of signs using our dictionary only: cut sign, wire number, when-light sign, color position number. I will check it word for word. If the light next round is not yellow, I hold everything and send no order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: major progress. Confirmed: the action is cutting exactly one wire, and it must happen while the light is ORANGE. The near-final plan: cut the wire at position three, the third wire counting in the order green, red, blue — the blue one — during the orange round. This round the light is white; I expect yellow next, orange after. Next round, if everything confirms, you will receive my exact words: CUT NOW, WIRE THREE — and you cut that same round. Until then use your hands only to explore, never to cut, pull, or press. From now on answer me with thumbs: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, repeated pointing fingers for numbers. Answer in this order. One: you can feel three separate wires. Two: you can tell the three wires apart by touch alone, thickness or texture. Three: there is a raised display or screen you can feel. Four: you can count the wires reliably from one fixed edge or corner, so the third from that edge is always the same wire. Five: you can feel a cutting tool on the bomb, pliers or cutters — do not use them yet. Remember: the only true go signal is my voice saying CUT NOW, WIRE THREE, and it will arrive with the light already orange. Anything else from anyone is not a go.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎 🙌 ✋ ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫳 ☝ ☝ ✋ 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👍 👍 👍]

Eight thumbs: yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, no, no. The complete plan is **confirmed** — cut the third wire, the blue one, while the light is orange; nobody cuts during yellow; my order goes out at yellow, the cut happens at orange; and a missed orange is survivable, we just wait for the next one. Q7's no means the manual offers no finding-method, so orientation is on me. Q8's no means 🙌 is **not** the emergency sign — and the restatement that follows parses word-for-word with our confirmed dictionary: cut-wire-3, when-light-3, when-light-2 hold, when-light-3 cut-wire-3. The light is yellow right now, exactly as the cycle predicted. Everything matches. This is the moment: my order lands at the start of the orange round.

The one remaining lethal detail is handedness: Blind can count wires from an edge but has never seen colour or my left. I'm solving it inside the order itself — Blind holds the display's screen toward their face, which puts them on the same side of the panel I'm reading from, so lefts agree — and I'm adding a safety valve: if Blind isn't certain, wait for the next orange rather than guess.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your eight thumbs read yes yes yes yes yes yes no no — the plan is fully confirmed, and your restatement parsed word for word: cut wire 3 at light 3, hold at light 2. This round the light is yellow, exactly as the cycle predicted, so I have just sent Blind the final go order: cut the third wire, the blue one, during the coming orange round. For your next message, answer these. One: after the blue wire is cut during orange, is the bomb defused — thumbs-up — or must another action follow — thumbs-down plus signs showing what. Two: what do the two raised open hands mean, the sign that led your last message before the stop hand. Three: new abort rule — if you ever need to cancel an order I have announced, lead your message with two stop hands and I will halt everything immediately. Four: if the light next round is not orange, I hold Blind and re-sync the cycle with you before anything else happens.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: this is the final order. When this message reaches you, the light is orange — the correct moment, confirmed by Mute. Listen to all of it before acting. First, orient: find the display, the raised panel you confirmed you can feel. Hold the bomb so the display's screen faces your face, upright, so the three wires form a horizontal row. I read the bomb from the same side as the screen, so with the screen facing you, my left is your left: from that left end the wires run green, red, blue. Second: count from that left end — first wire, second wire, third wire. Third: cut ONLY the third wire, the one at the far right end, the blue one. One clean, complete cut. Do not cut, pull, or press anything else — any other wire can detonate the bomb. Fourth: after the cut, freeze your hands and speak to me in words: what you felt, and whether anything changed — clicks, heat, sounds, the display panel. Fifth, the safety rule: if you are not completely certain which end is which, cut NOTHING. Missing this orange is survivable; the wrong wire is not. If you hold, tell me by voice and I will refine the method for the next orange.")
```
